subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In botany, a carnivorous plant is one that derives nutrients by trapping and digesting insects.
• Charles Darwin first studied carnivorous plants systematically in the 1870s.
• Carnivorous plants obtain nutrients when they capture, digest, or absorb prey.
• A Venus flytrap is a plant with hinged leaves that can snap shut.
• A Venus flytrap can capture insects when trigger hairs on its leaves detect movement and cause the trap to close.
prompt: The student wants to provide an explanation and an example of carnivorous plants. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Carnivorous plants obtain nutrients through different prey-based processes; for example, some obtain nutrients by capturing insects.
choices.B: Capturing, digesting, and absorbing are three examples of how carnivorous plants and Venus flytraps can obtain nutrients from prey.
choices.C: Carnivorous plants—plants that derive nutrients by trapping and digesting insects—include the Venus flytrap, a plant whose hinged leaves snap shut to capture prey.
choices.D: A Venus flytrap is a plant that obtains nutrients from insects, a feeding strategy that Charles Darwin studied systematically in the 1870s.

explanation: Choice C is the best answer. The sentence provides an explanation and an example of carnivorous plants, explaining that they are plants that derive nutrients by trapping and digesting insects and offering the Venus flytrap as an example.
